title: sast-corpus ground-truth case
description: One labelled case. This file is the ONLY place the answer may appear; the fixture it points at must contain no hint of its own label or category.

id.description: Opaque identifier. Deliberately carries no semantic content — an id that hints at the category defeats the corpus.

label.description: 'safe' marks a false-positive trap: plausible-looking code that is genuinely not a vulnerability. A finding here is an FP.

plane.description: Which detection plane this case exercises. Planes are scored independently.

tier.description: 1 = synthetic micro-fixture, 2 = real open-source application, 3 = real CVE reproduction. Always reported separately: tier-1-only numbers overstate every tool.

framework.description: e.g. spring-mvc, django, express, nestjs, laravel, rails, gin. Null for plain-language cases.

primary_cwe.description: The single most precise CWE for this case.

acceptable_cwes.description: Every CWE a scanner could reasonably report for this flaw. Must include primary_cwe. Scoring a tool down for choosing a defensible sibling CWE measures taxonomy preference, not detection.

location.description: Primary expected report location — normally the sink.

alt_locations.description: Other defensible report locations, normally the source. A hit at any one of these counts as a match, so tools that report at the head of a taint chain are not penalised.

difficulty.description: What makes this case hard. Enables 'tool X handles intra-procedural flow but collapses on inter-file' instead of a single opaque percentage.

flow.description: `unknown` is honest for a derived tier-3 case: the taint path is not known until someone reads the code, and a guess would be indistinguishable from a finding in the difficulty breakdown.

sanitizer.description: custom-effective and framework-implicit are the usual causes of false positives; 'ineffective' is a sanitizer that looks right but is not.

obfuscation.description: How far the flow is from a direct source-to-sink chain. `strong-update` is a false-positive trap rather than a difficulty: the variable is overwritten with a safe value before the sink, and a tool that does not model overwriting reports a vulnerability that is not there. `container-field` holds the taint in an object field and passes the object around.

rationale.description: Why this label is correct. A reviewer must be able to check the call without re-deriving the analysis.

required.description: True if this case must compile for build-required engines (Fortify, Coverity, Veracode) to see it at all.

recipe.description: Path to the hermetic build script, relative to repo root.

secret.description: Extra ground truth for plane: secret.

sca.description: Extra ground truth for plane: sca.

variant.description: The specific mechanism this case exercises within its CWE. One case per CWE only proves a tool knows the class exists; variants are where tools separate. For CWE-89: concat-statement, prepared-but-concatenated, dynamic-identifier, format-string, orm-raw-fragment, second-order. Also names context traps, where the same token in a different place is not a finding: in-markdown, in-comment, in-test-data, in-vendored, in-example-config.

retired.description: Why this case stopped being scored. Present means retired: the case leaves the answer key but the file stays, so a scorecard produced against an earlier corpus version remains explainable. A string, never a boolean — `retired: true` records that someone stopped trusting the case and not why, and the why is the part a later reader needs.

file.description: Repo-relative path, forward slashes. Must live under a corpus tier.
